name: Curcumin
summary: The main yellow compound in turmeric, taken mostly for joint pain and inflammation; evidence is preliminary, and turmeric supplements have been linked to rare liver injury.
what_it_is: Turmeric (Curcuma longa) is a plant in the ginger family grown mainly in India and Southeast Asia; its underground stem (rhizome) is used in cooking and was used in traditional medicine for indigestion, colds, skin infections, arthritis and liver disease. Curcumin, which gives turmeric its yellow color, belongs to a group of compounds called curcuminoids that are thought to account for its effects. Products vary in how much curcumin they contain, and many add piperine from black pepper, which raises how much curcumin the body absorbs; piperine was in 3 of 7 products tested in US liver-injury cases.

evidence.why: Several meta-analyses of small trials suggest less knee osteoarthritis pain, but NIH says higher-quality studies are needed and there isn't enough evidence to confirm any health benefit.

status_us.label: Dietary supplement; also a common spice
status_us.note: Sold as a dietary supplement and widely used as a cooking spice. Supplements are not approved by FDA before they are sold; manufacturers are responsible for their safety and labeling.

benefits.claim: Less knee osteoarthritis pain and better function than placebo, similar to NSAID pain relievers, in a 2021 review of 10 studies (1,287 people); NIH calls this initial evidence that needs higher-quality confirmation
Less muscle soreness and lower muscle-damage markers after exercise in a 2020 review of 11 studies
Some benefit in early studies of fatty liver disease, though it is unclear which measures improve consistently

risks.risk: Liver injury, usually starting 1 to 4 months after beginning a turmeric supplement; of 10 US cases in a national registry, 5 people were hospitalized and 1 died of liver failure. Cases have risen since 2011 and are strongly linked to the gene variant HLA-B*35:01
Stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, acid reflux, diarrhea or constipation
Turmeric supplements may be unsafe in pregnancy, and a professional monograph advises avoiding them while pregnant or breastfeeding
Long-term safety is unknown; it is usually well tolerated in short studies, but the rare liver injuries typically began 1 to 4 months after starting
Bleeding: it may add to the effect of blood thinners, antiplatelet drugs and NSAIDs, and one case report described a sudden rise in INR on warfarin
Hives or itching when used on the skin

avoid_if: Gallstones or a blocked bile duct
Liver disease or past liver injury from a supplement (clinician first)
Bleeding disorder, upcoming surgery, or taking a blood thinner (clinician first)
interactions: Blood thinners, antiplatelet drugs and NSAIDs (such as warfarin, apixaban, aspirin or ibuprofen): possible added bleeding risk
Medicines cleared by the liver enzymes CYP3A or CYP2D6 (such as tacrolimus): turmeric may raise their levels; a case report linked it to high tacrolimus levels

Piperine (black pepper extract): often added to raise curcumin absorption; it was in 3 of 7 products tested in US liver-injury cases, and researchers suggest the combination may help explain rising cases

labs.why: No routine tests are needed, but tiredness, dark urine or yellow skin or eyes should prompt stopping it and calling a clinician, who may check liver tests.

studies.title: Therapeutic effects of turmeric or curcumin extract on pain and function for individuals with knee osteoarthritis
studies.people: 1,287 people with knee osteoarthritis in 10 studies
studies.finding: Turmeric or curcumin may improve knee pain and function compared with placebo, with effects similar to NSAIDs; the best amount, frequency and form remain unclear. Summarized by NIH; the paper itself was not opened.

studies.title: Liver Injury Associated with Turmeric-A Growing Problem: Ten Cases from the Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network [DILIN]
studies.people: 10 people with liver injury in a US registry (2004 to 2022)
studies.finding: Injury was mostly of the liver-cell (hepatocellular) type and began 1 to 4 months after starting; 5 were hospitalized and 1 died. Seven of the 10 carried HLA-B*35:01, and the authors say cases appear to be increasing.

ask_your_clinician: Is curcumin likely to help my joint pain, and how would we judge whether it is working?
Which liver symptoms should make me stop it and call you?
Could it interact with any of my medicines?

notes_for_editor: NIH's turmeric page (April 2025) says there isn't enough evidence to confirm any benefit. The osteoarthritis and exercise-soreness review details come through NIH's 2022 clinical digest, not the papers themselves. LiverTox's turmeric chapter, a USP review of turmeric-related liver injury and a 2022 knee osteoarthritis meta-analysis on PMC could not be opened (bot checks). The DILIN series is small and from one registry; HLA-B*35:01 testing is not routine. Interactions, the gallstone contraindication and the pregnancy advice were added in review from the Drugs.com professional monograph (Nov 2025); the warfarin INR rise is a single case report. Brand-name formulations in the catalog aliases are not mentioned. The gut goal is used for inflammation.
